BURHAN:v3p437/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p437/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p437/r2.claim: In بل نقذف بالحق على الباطل فيدمغه, both throwing and crushing are metaphorical expressions.

JISHUMI:v5p3579/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3579/r3.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v5p3579/r3.claim: Abū Muslim links the promise of good overcoming evil to the statement that truth is hurled against falsehood and crushes it.
JISHUMI:v5p3579/r3.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى: (بل نقذف بالحق على الباطل فيدمغه)

BURSEVI:v5p353/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p353/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p353/r1.claim: The passage turns from denying a child to God's usual action: He makes truth—seriousness, faith, and Quran—overcome falsehood such as play, disbelief, and other vanities.
BURSEVI:v5p353/r1.anchor: بل شأننا أن نغلب الحق الذي من جملته الجد والإيمان والقرآن

BURSEVI:v5p353/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p353/r2.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v5p353/r2.claim: Qadhf is a forceful throw over a distance, and falsehood is the opposite of truth because it has no stability when exposed.
BURSEVI:v5p353/r2.anchor: القذف الرمي البعيد ولاعتبار البعد فيه

BURSEVI:v5p353/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p353/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p353/r3.claim: Yadmugh means to destroy and eliminate.
BURSEVI:v5p353/r3.anchor: قال أهل التفسير إنما استعار لذلك أي :

BURSEVI:v5p353/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p353/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
BURSEVI:v5p353/r4.claim: They explain the image as a hard projectile of truth crushing hollow, soft falsehood like a brain struck through its membrane, making falsehood perish.
BURSEVI:v5p353/r4.anchor: قال أهل التفسير إنما استعار لذلك

BURSEVI:v5p353/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p353/r5.speaker: صاحب المفتاح
BURSEVI:v5p353/r5.claim: Qadhf and damgh first refer to bodies, then metaphorically to presenting truth to falsehood and erasing it; the sensory image makes the abstract scene vivid.
BURSEVI:v5p353/r5.anchor: قال "صاحب المفتاح" : أصل استعمال القذف والدمغ في الأجسام

BURSEVI:v5p353/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p353/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p353/r6.claim: The sudden particle and nominal sentence in fa-idha huwa zahiq signal how swiftly and completely falsehood disappears; the death image reinforces the metaphor.
BURSEVI:v5p353/r6.anchor: وفي إذا المفاجأة والجملة الإسمية من الدلالة على كمال المسارعة

BURSEVI:v5p353/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p353/r7.speaker: نجم الدين
BURSEVI:v5p353/r7.claim: There are three levels: God's commands defeat forbidden acts, manifestation of His attributes defeats servantly attributes, and manifestation of His Essence defeats all created essences.
BURSEVI:v5p353/r7.anchor: للحق ثلاث مراتب وكذا للباطل مرتبة أفعال الحق

BURSEVI:v5p353/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p353/r8.speaker: المغربي
BURSEVI:v5p353/r8.claim: The ecstatic utterance أنا الحق is explained as spoken when manifestation of the divine Essence or attribute makes the speaker's own false self vanish.
BURSEVI:v5p353/r8.anchor: لعل من قال أنا الحق إنما قال عند تجلي ذات الحق

BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r1.speaker: المغربي
BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r1.claim: His verse presents the speaker of أنا الحق as the servant whose defender and victor is the manifest Real.
BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r1.anchor: ناصر ومنصور ميكويد انا الحق المبين بشنواز ناصركه آن كفتار

BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r2.speaker: الخجندي
BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r2.claim: His verse associates hearing the secret أنا الحق with self-annihilation at the gallows of extinction.
BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r2.anchor: وقال الخجندي قدس سره : هركه بدار فنا جبه هستى بسوخت

BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r3.speaker: الخجندي
BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r3.claim: He says the secret of أنا الحق is lofty and cannot be understood without paying its price.
BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r3.anchor: أسرار أنا الحق سخهن نيك بلندست معنى نين جز بسردار نيابى

BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r4.speaker: الأصمعي
BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r4.claim: Wayl can mean ugliness or woe and can express lament; ways is belittling and wayh expresses compassion.
BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r4.anchor: قال الأصمعي ويل قبوح وقد يستعمل في التحسر وويس استصغار

BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r5.claim: Those who call wayl a valley in Hell mean that the people God describes with it deserve a settled place in the Fire, not that this is the word's lexical meaning.
BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r5.anchor: ومن قال ويل واد في جهنم فإنه لم يرد أن ويلا في اللغة

BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p353#2/r6.claim: The polytheists are threatened with ruin because of their descriptions of God as having a woman or child and their accusations that revelation is magic, confused dreams, or similar falsehoods.

SULAMI:v2p5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p5/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p5/r1.claim: For spiritual elders, admonition can take the form of Truth being cast against falsehood and crushing it.
SULAMI:v2p5/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : الوعظ للأكابر . ومنهم من له مشار مقذوف

SULAMI:v2p5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p5/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p5/r2.claim: For spiritual elders, admonition can take the form of Truth being cast against falsehood and crushing it.
SULAMI:v2p5/r2.anchor: كقوله : ﴿ بل نقذف بالحق على الباطل فيدمغه ﴾

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p285#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p285#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p285#2/r1.claim: فيدمغه means he smashes it; the root concerns striking the head or brain, a fatal blow.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p285#2/r1.anchor: أصل هذا إصابة الرأس والدماغ بالضرب

NAHHAS:v3p67/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p67/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p67/r1.claim: Truth is cast with proofs and arguments against falsehood, identified as their claim; زاهق means broken down and vanished.
NAHHAS:v3p67/r1.anchor: أي بالحجج والبراهين ( على الباطل ) وهو قولهم ( فإذا هو زاهق

NAHHAS:v3p67/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p67/r2.speaker: أهل اللغة
NAHHAS:v3p67/r2.claim: Linguists use زهق يزهق زهقا and زهوقا for breaking down and disappearing.
NAHHAS:v3p67/r2.anchor: حكى أهل اللغة زهق يزهق زهقا وزهوقا إذا انكسر واضمحل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r1.claim: بل invalidates the idea that creation is play and advances the stronger point that God actively strikes down falsehood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r1.anchor: بل نحن نعمد إلى باطلكم فنقذف بالحق عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r2.claim: Throwing truth is a metaphor for whatever abolishes falsehood: proof, warning, destruction, or a created force that overcomes it; God also grants discernment and may empower servants against wrongdoers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r2.anchor: يبطل الباطل بالحق بأن يبين للناس بطلان الباطل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r3.claim: دمغ first means breaking a hard hollow body, then extends the throwing metaphor to the annihilation of falsehood; both images transfer the physical to the intellectual.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r3.anchor: استعير الدمغ لمحق الباطل وإزالته كما يزيل القذف الجسم المقذوف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r4.claim: The suddenness particle depicts truth's swift victory once it arrives clearly, since truth has force and acts quickly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r4.anchor: ودل حرف المفاجأة على سرعة محق الحق الباطل عند وروده لأن للحق صولة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r5.claim: زاهق means displaced and perishing; Ibn Ashur notes its verb forms and parallels its use for souls and falsehood elsewhere.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r6.claim: After the preceding argument against their claims about the Messenger and Quran, the passage ends by cursing them for what they allege about Muhammad and the Quran.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v17p33/r6.anchor: وعندما انتهت مقارعتهم بالحجج الساطعة لإبطال قولهم في الرسول وفي القرآن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p77/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p77/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p77/r4.claim: Al-ḥaqq includes the Qurʾan, the message, the law, and all truth; al-bāṭil likewise covers falsehood generally.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p77/r4.anchor: «الحق» عام في القرآن والرسالة والشرع وكل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p77/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p77/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p77/r5.claim: Yadmughuhu means to strike the brain, a fatal blow in humans; likewise truth destroys falsehood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p77/r5.anchor: ويدمغه معناه يصيب دماغه وذلك مهلك في البشر فكذلك الحق يهلك الباطل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p77/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p77/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p77/r6.claim: Wayl can mean disgrace and grief or the name of a valley in Hell, which is the intended sense if the latter view is adopted.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p77/r6.anchor: والويل الخزي والهم وقيل هو اسم واد في جهنم فهو المراد في هذه الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p77/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p77/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p77/r7.claim: The warning addresses disbelievers who ascribed to God what is improper and unfitting.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p77/r7.anchor: وهذه مخاطبة للكفار الذين وصفوا الله تعالى بما لا يجوز عليه ولا يليق به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p344/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p344/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p344/r1.claim: “Rather” dismisses their false claim: God casts the Qurʾanic truth upon their lie and crushes it; Ibn Qutayba derives the image from a lethal blow to the brain, and the falsehood vanishes.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p344/r1.anchor: نقذف بالحق أي نسلط الحق وهو القرآن على الباطل وهو كذبهم فيدمغه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p344/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p344/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p344/r2.claim: Commentators explain that God invalidates their falsehood with the truth until it disappears; woe is due for describing God with what is improper.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p344/r2.anchor: إنا نبطل كذبهم بما نثبين من الحق حتى يضمحل ولكم الويل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p336/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p336/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p336/r3.claim: God makes truth plain so it defeats and erases falsehood; the warning condemns those who claim God has a child and their false assertions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p336/r3.anchor: نبين الحق فيدحض الباطل؛ ولهذا قال

JISHUMI:v7p4794/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4794/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4794/r2.claim: Zāhiq can mean one that perishes, but also a fat or stout animal; “his soul departed” is another usage.
JISHUMI:v7p4794/r2.anchor: والزاهق من الأضداد، يقال للهالك زاهق، والسمين من الدواب زاهق

JISHUMI:v7p4794/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4794/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4794/r4.claim: Damag means striking the head through to the brain, and by extension destroying; the Prophet is described as the breaker of hosts of falsehood.
JISHUMI:v7p4794/r4.anchor: والدمغ: شج الرأس حتى يبلغ الدماغ، يقال: دمغه يدمغه دمغا

JISHUMI:v7p4801/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4801/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4801/r1.claim: The truth is distinguished from falsehood by proofs, which makes the image of casting truth onto falsehood appropriate.
JISHUMI:v7p4801/r1.anchor: هاتوا برهانكم أي: حجتكم على ذلك

JISHUMI:v7p4801/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4801/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v7p4801/r2.claim: The question about earthly gods links to the command to ask the People of the Reminder: ask whether messengers were ever other than men and whether earthly idols can create; all messengers called to God's oneness.
JISHUMI:v7p4801/r2.anchor: إنه يتصل بقوله: (فاسألوا أهل الذكر) أي: سلهم هل أرسل قبلك إلا رجالا

JISHUMI:v7p4801/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4801/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4801/r3.claim: Another coherence reading connects the claim about taking amusement to the opponents' attribution of a child and partner to God.
JISHUMI:v7p4801/r3.anchor: يتصل بقوله: (لو أردنا أن نتخذ لهوا) أي: أضافوا إليه الولد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p108/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p108/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p108/r1.claim: Bal rejects amusement and exalts God above it: wisdom and self-sufficiency lead Him to overcome play with seriousness and defeat falsehood with truth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p108/r1.anchor: {بل } إضراب عن اتخاذ اللهو واللعب ، وتنزيه منه لذاته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p108/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p108/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p108/r2.claim: Casting and crushing are metaphors for annihilating falsehood, pictured as a hard stone crushing a soft, hollow object.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p108/r2.anchor: واستعار لذلك القذف والدمغ ، تصويرا لإبطاله وإهداره ومحقه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p108/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p108/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p108/r3.claim: An accusative reading of fa-yadmagh is judged weak, like the cited poetic subjunctive construction.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p108/r3.anchor: وقرىء : ( فيدمغه ) بالنصب ، وهو في ضعف قوله : سأترك منزلي لبني تميم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r3.claim: One interpretation makes truth the followed word and falsehood the rejected one; yadmugh means erase and destroy, like a lethal wound at the crown of the head.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r3.anchor: أن الحق الكلام المتبوع , والباطل المدفوع . ومعنى يدمغه أي يذهبه ويهلكه

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, truth means the Qur'an and falsehood means Iblīs.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r5.speaker: بعض أهل الخواطر
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r5.claim: One contemplative interpretation makes truth admonitions and falsehood sins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r5.anchor: أن الحق المواعظ والباطل المعاصي , قاله بعض أهل الخواطر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r6.claim: A further possible interpretation makes truth Islam and falsehood polytheism.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r6.anchor: ويحتمل رابعا : أن الحق الإسلام , والباطل الشرك

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r8.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p440#2/r8.claim: Zāhiq means going away or disappearing.

MUQATIL:21:16-18/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:21:16-18/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:21:16-18/r2.claim: Against Najran Christians’ claim that Jesus is God’s son, God says a child, if intended, would be taken from the angels; He does not beget one, and truth smashes their falsehood.
MUQATIL:21:16-18/r2.anchor: وذلك أن نصارى نجران السيد والعاقب، ومن معهما، قالوا: عيسى ابن الله،

NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r1.claim: The verse turns away from any thought that God takes amusement, declaring instead that His practice is to cast truth upon falsehood.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r1.anchor: بل اضراب عن اتخاذ اللهو وتنزيه منه لذاته كأنه قال سبحاننا أن نتخذ اللهو

NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r2.claim: Truth may be the Qurʾān, Islam against idolatry, or earnestness against play; falsehood may mean Satan or idolatry.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r2.anchor: ﴿ بالحق ﴾ بالقرآن ﴿ على الباطل ﴾ الشيطان أو بالإسلام على ا لشرك أو بالجد على اللعب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r3.claim: Yadmaghu means breaks and overcomes; falsehood then departs and perishes.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r4.claim: Casting and striking the head are a subtle bodily metaphor: strong truth strikes weak falsehood and makes it perish.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r4.anchor: وهذه استعارة لطيفة لأن أصل استعمال القذف والدمغ في الاجسام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r5.claim: The verse closes by condemning their attribution of a child and other claims to God.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p76#6/r5.anchor: ﴿ ولكم الويل مما تصفون ﴾ الله به من الولد ونحوه

SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r1.claim: The common reading raises the final غ as coordination; Isa ibn Umar reads it in the accusative, which al-Zamakhshari calls weak and likens to a poetic line.
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r1.anchor: العامة على رفع الغين نسقا على ما قبله. وقرأ عيسى بن عمر بنصبها. قال الزمخشري: " وهو في ضعف

SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r2.claim: A rare reading with ḍamma on م may reflect two imperfect dialects or a ḍamma assimilated from the guttural consonant.
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r2.anchor: وقرىء شاذا " فيدمغه " بضم الميم، وهي محتملة لأن يكون في المضارع لغتان

SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r3.claim: يدمغه means strike the brain; دمغت الرجل means hit him in the brain, like verbs naming a struck body part.
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r3.anchor: ويدمغه: أي يصيب دماغه، من قولهم دمغت الرجل أي: ضربته في دماغه

SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r4.claim: مما تصفون may attach to an implied استقرار with causal من, meaning woe is fixed for you because of what you describe.
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r4.anchor: أحدها: أنه متعلق بالاستقرار الذي تعلق به الخبر أي: استقر لكم الويل من أجل ما تصفون

SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r5.claim: He takes مما تصفون as a circumstantial phrase qualifying الويل: woe coming upon them because of their descriptions.
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r5.anchor: والثالث: أنه حال من الويل أي: الويل واقعا مما تصفون، كذا قدره أبو البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r6.claim: ما can be a verbal noun without a resumptive pronoun, or relative/indefinite-relative, in which case a pronoun is required but omitted under the relevant conditions.
SAMIN-DURR:21:18/r6.anchor: و " ما " في { مما تصفون } يجوز أن تكون مصدرية فلا عائد عند الجمهور، وأن تكون بمعنى الذي

RAZI-FULL:v22p127#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p127#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p127#2/r6.claim: “Rather” turns away from taking amusement or play: divine wisdom defeats play with seriousness and falsehood with truth, depicted as a hard projectile battering a soft body.
RAZI-FULL:v22p127#2/r6.anchor: تصويرا لإبطاله فجعله كأنه جرم صلب كالصخرة مثلا قذف به

RAZI-FULL:v22p127#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p127#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p127#2/r7.claim: The threat of woe addresses those who reject the Messenger and call the Qur’an magic, confused dreams, and other falsehoods.
RAZI-FULL:v22p127#2/r7.anchor: من تمسك بتكذيب الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم ونسب القرآن إلى أنه سحر وأضغاث أحلام

STUDYQURAN:21:18/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r1.claim: Damagha can mean overcoming or vanquishing, but evokes skull-crushing to the brain and can also mean stamping a form into soft material.
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r1.anchor: Crushes renders the verb damagha, a word that can have the general sense of overcoming or vanquishing

STUDYQURAN:21:18/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r2.claim: Ṭ understands vanishing as meaning that falsehood is destroyed.
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r2.anchor: Vanishes is understood by some to mean “is destroyed” (Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:21:18/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r3.claim: The Quran discusses the relationship between truth and falsehood elsewhere, including truth's triumph and God's verification of truth.
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r3.anchor: The relationship between falsehood and truth in the Quran is discussed at greater length in the commentary on 17:81

STUDYQURAN:21:18/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r4.claim: That which the wrongdoers describe may refer to the lies they tell.
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r4.anchor: That which you describe can either refer to the lies the wrongdoers told

STUDYQURAN:21:18/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r5.claim: Alternatively, the phrase may refer to idolatry and the partners attributed to God.
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r5.anchor: or signify their idolatry, recalling phrases such as Exalted is God above the partners they ascribe

STUDYQURAN:21:18/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r6.claim: The indictment also recalls the closing appeal to God for help against what people ascribe to Him.
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r6.anchor: see also v. 112, where God is said to be the One Whose help is sought against that which you ascribe

STUDYQURAN:21:18/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r7.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r7.claim: Some understand the descriptions as the accusations against the Prophet in verses 3–5.
STUDYQURAN:21:18/r7.anchor: Some understand these descriptions to refer to the accusations made against the Prophet in vv. 3–5.

TAB-FULL:v16p240/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p240/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p240/r1.claim: God sends down His Book and revelation as truth against denial; it destroys falsehood as a blow to the head reaching the brain kills its victim, leaving falsehood vanished.
TAB-FULL:v16p240/r1.anchor: الدماغ، وإذا بلغت الشجة ذلك من المشجوج لم يكن له بعدها حياة

TAB-FULL:v16p240/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p240/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p240/r2.claim: Qatada calls the truth God's Qur'an and falsehood Satan, which the truth drives away; he also glosses vanishing as destruction or departure.
TAB-FULL:v16p240/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {بل نقذف بالحق على الباطل فيدمغه فإذا هو زاهق} [الأنبياء: 18] والحق كتاب الله القرآن

TAB-FULL:v16p241/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p241/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p241/r1.claim: The threatened woe is for describing God falsely as having a wife or child and fabricating claims about Him; lying and associating partners both fit, but the nearest wording to audience understanding is preferable.
TAB-FULL:v16p241/r1.anchor: فمتفقة معانيه، لأن من وصف الله بأن له صاحبة فقد كذب

TAB-FULL:v16p241/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p241/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p241/r2.claim: Qatada says the false descriptions are lies.
TAB-FULL:v16p241/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ولكم الويل مما تصفون} [الأنبياء: 18] أي تكذبون

TAB-FULL:v16p241/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p241/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v16p241/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the descriptions amount to associating partners with God; he gives the same gloss for 21:22 and reports Mujahid's gloss of 6:139 as lying.
TAB-FULL:v16p241/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج: {ولكم الويل مما تصفون} [الأنبياء: 18] قال: تشركون

ZAJJAJ:v3p387/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p387/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p387/r1.claim: The truth hurled against falsehood is the Qur’an; it crushes and removes falsehood with humiliation.
ZAJJAJ:v3p387/r1.anchor:
يعنى بالحق القرآن على باطلهم
" فيدمغه " فيذهبه ذهاب الصغار والإذلال.

ZAJJAJ:v3p387/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p387/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p387/r3.claim: Their وصف of God as having a son is a lie, and woe is due for that false description.
ZAJJAJ:v3p387/r3.anchor:
(ولكم الويل مما تصفون).
أي مما تكذبون في وصفكم في قولكم إن لله ولدا.

TABATABAI:21:18/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:18/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:18/r1.claim: Qadhf is throwing at a distance, damgh is a head wound reaching the brain, and zahūq is perishing; truth has real stability, whereas falsehood only resembles truth, as water differs from a mirage.
TABATABAI:21:18/r1.anchor: والدمغ - على ما في مجمع البيان - شج الرأس حتى يبلغ الدماغ

TABATABAI:21:18/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:18/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:18/r2.claim: The Qur'an treats factual beliefs and the afterlife as truth, worldly possessions and secondary causes as falsehood, and God alone as absolute truth.
TABATABAI:21:18/r2.anchor: وعد الحياة الآخرة حقا والحياة الدنيا بجميع ما يراه الإنسان لنفسه فيها ويسعى له سعيه من ملك

TABATABAI:21:18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:18/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:18/r3.claim: Falsehood arises as a deficiency relative to something more complete, and is related to God only by permission; a salt flat that appears like water illustrates a merely imagined mirage.
TABATABAI:21:18/r3.anchor: فليس ينتسب إليه بالاستقامة وإنما هو لازم نقص بعض الأشياء

TABATABAI:21:18#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:18#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:18#2/r1.claim: All existence has some admixture of falsehood, while God is pure truth; the created order's mixture is illustrated by the rainwater and foam parable.
TABATABAI:21:18#2/r1.anchor: أن الله هو الحق النور 24، ويظهر أيضا أن الخلقة على ما فيها من النظام

TABATABAI:21:18#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:18#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:18#2/r2.claim: God's continuing practice is to give falsehood time, then cast truth upon it so that it vanishes; truth's beliefs, perfection, and prophetic victory endure even against few followers or severe opposition.
TABATABAI:21:18#2/r2.anchor: وقد جرت سنة الله تعالى أن يمهل الباطل حتى إذا اعترض الحق ليبطله

TABATABAI:21:18#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:18#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:18#2/r3.claim: The repeated verb signals an ongoing law, truth's casting on falsehood signals superiority, and the sudden vanishing signals a surprising reversal; the rule is unrestricted across belief, practice, and creation.
TABATABAI:21:18#2/r3.anchor: المفيد للاستمرار دلالة على كونه سنة جارية

TABATABAI:21:18#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:18#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:21:18#2/r4.claim: Some interpret the verse as saying that God sets earnestness, as a kind of truth, against amusement, but Tabataba'i rejects this because it assumes divine amusement which the preceding passage denied.
TABATABAI:21:18#2/r4.anchor: لكنا لا نريد اتخاذ اللهو بل شأننا أن نغلب الحق الذي من جملته الجد

TABATABAI:21:18#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:18#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:18#2/r5.claim: The warning is directed at those who deny resurrection and prophethood; return to God means God continuously purifies truth from whatever obscures it until only the absolute truth remains.

TABATABAI:21:16-33#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:16-33#4/r1.speaker: يونس
TABATABAI:21:16-33#4/r1.claim: Al-Maḥasin transmits a raised report from Yunus quoting al-Sadiq: whenever falsehood confronts truth, truth overcomes it; this is the meaning of the verse.
TABATABAI:21:16-33#4/r1.anchor: عن يونس رفعه قال قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام ليس من باطل يقوم بإزاء حق إلا غلب الحق الباطل

TABATABAI:21:16-33#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:16-33#4/r2.speaker: أيوب بن الحر
TABATABAI:21:16-33#4/r2.claim: A second al-Sadiq report says truth comes to every person and breaks the heart of whoever accepts or leaves it; Tabataba'i says both reports generalize the verse.
TABATABAI:21:16-33#4/r2.anchor: عن أيوب بن الحر قال قال أبو عبد الله عليه السلام يا أيوب ما من أحد إلا وقد يرد عليه الحق

TABATABAI:21:16-33#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:21:16-33#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:21:16-33#4/r3.claim: The two reports apply the verse broadly rather than limiting it to one historical contest.

TABRISI:21:14-18/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:14-18/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:14-18/r14.claim: God instead brings decisive proofs against falsehood; alternatives describe argument against doubt or faith against disbelief.
TABRISI:21:14-18/r14.anchor: معناه بل نورد الأدلة القاهرة على الباطل

TABRISI:21:14-18/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:14-18/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:14-18/r15.claim: Yadmaghuhu means that truth overcomes and invalidates falsehood, or destroys it; zāhiq means perishing and vanishing, as Qatada explains.

TABRISI:21:14-18/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:21:14-18/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:21:14-18/r16.claim: God manifests truth with proofs and defeats falsehood, so He cannot be the one playing falsehood; the disbelievers deserve ruin for attributing spouse and child to Him.
TABRISI:21:14-18/r16.anchor: يظهر الحق بأدلته ويبطل الباطل فكيف يفعل الباطل واللعب

ASAD-NOTES:21:18#n20/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:18#n20/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:18#n20/r1.claim: The truth being cast against falsehood is God’s transcendence, which rejects the idea that God is immanent in or coexists with creation.
ASAD-NOTES:21:18#n20/r1.anchor: the truth of God's transcendence against the false idea of His existential immanence

ASAD-NOTES:21:18#n21/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:18#n21/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:18#n21/r1.claim: The finite, perishable universe cannot be a projection of its Creator, who is infinite and eternal.
ASAD-NOTES:21:18#n21/r1.anchor: The obvious fact that everything in the created universe is finite and perishable effectively refutes

ASAD-NOTES:21:18#n22/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:21:18#n22/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:21:18#n22/r1.claim: The phrase about what people attribute to God also means defining Him; treating God as immanent in creation attempts to define His Being.
ASAD-NOTES:21:18#n22/r1.anchor: the idea of God's "immanence" in His creation is equivalent to an attempt to define His Being

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r1.claim: Bal rejects the opponents’ claim and description of God as false; the verse says truth is cast over their falsehood until it removes it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r1.anchor: بل" (¬8) هاهنا: إبطال لكلامهم [ووصفهم الله] (¬9) بما لا يجوز. يقول: دع ذلك فإنه باطل كذب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r2.claim: Qadhf means to throw; here God causes truth to overpower and be cast upon their falsehood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r2.anchor: قذف بالشيء (¬10)، إذا رمى به (¬11). أي: نسلط الحق # على باطلهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq identifies the truth cast down as the Qurʾān and the falsehood as their lies.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r3.anchor: يعني بالحق القرآن (¬1)، على باطلهم (¬2)] (¬3) وهو كذبهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r4.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī glosses yadmughuhu as destroying it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba says it means to break; its root image is a blow to the brain, a fatal strike.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r5.anchor: ابن قتيبة: يكسره. وأصل هذا إصابة الدماغ بالضرب وهو مقتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r6.claim: Abū Isḥāq explains the defeat as making falsehood disappear through abasement and humiliation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r7.claim: Zāhiq means vanishing or going away.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās compares falsehood’s departure to an arrow leaving its target.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r9.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r9.anchor: وقال قتادة: هالك (¬10). وذكرنا هذا عند قوله: {وزهق الباطل} [الإسراء: 81]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r10.claim: The truth makes their lies clear, so their falsehood dwindles and disappears; the discussion links this wording to the verse saying falsehood vanishes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r10.anchor: نبطل كذبهم بما تبين من الحق حتى يضمحل (¬2) ويذهب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r11.claim: Al-wayl can mean a valley in Hell, and here threatens the unbelievers for their lies and impermissible descriptions of God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r11.anchor: ابن عباس: يريد واديا في جهنم (¬3)، يقول لكم يا معشر الكفار الويل من كذبكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r12.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r12.claim: Mujāhid glosses what they describe as what they lie about, linking the expression to God’s recompense for their description.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r13.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r13.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r13.claim: The particular lie is their claim that God has a child.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r13.anchor: مما تكذبون في وصفكم # الله بأن له ولدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r14.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r14.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r14.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the warning applies until the Resurrection to anyone who makes a false description.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r14.anchor: الحسن في هذه الآية: هي والله (¬2) لكل واصف كذب (¬3) إلى يوم القيامة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r15.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r15.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r15.claim: Anyone who falsely describes God’s attributes or rulings falls under this warning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p39/r15.anchor: من وصف كذبا على الله في صفاته وأحكامه (¬5)، فهو من أهل هذه الآية

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:16-21/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:16-21/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:21:16-21/r3.claim: God casts the Quranic truth against the disbelievers’ falsehood, demolishing it until it vanishes; they face woe for attributing unworthy things to God.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p302/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p302/r10.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p302/r10.claim: The truth cast against falsehood is the Quran.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p303/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p303/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p303/r1.claim: Falsehood means the polytheists’ shirk; Qatada says the truth cast against it is God’s Book, and “demolishes” means defeats and vanishes.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p303/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p303/r2.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p303/r2.claim: The disbelievers face punishment for claiming that the angels are God’s daughters; this is their lie.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p303/r2.anchor: قال قتادة: مما تكذبون، لقولهم: إن الملائكة بنات الله.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:18/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:18/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:18/r1.claim: By metaphor, God says falsehood cannot remain where truth is present: it is struck down and vanishes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:21:18/r1.anchor: Allah Teâlâ, hakkın bulunduğu yerde bâtılın barınamayacağını, yok olup gideceğini mecazi bir anlatımla ifade

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r2.claim: The universe is not amusement: its just, wise Creator will establish a day when truth prevails and falsehood is defeated.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r2.anchor: it is essential that He bring about a day in which the truth is victorious and falsehood is vanquished

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r3.claim: Multiple gods with separate wills would make the universe unsustainable; the prophets all taught monotheism, with no trace of polytheism in their teachings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r3.anchor: If there had been multiple gods of this universe having their own will and intention, it would not have survived

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r4.claim: Angels are God's honourable servants, not daughters or autonomous intercessors; they speak only with His permission, and anyone claiming partnership with God faces Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p91/r4.anchor: Angels are not daughters of God; they are His honourable servants. They cannot even utter a word before Him without His permission

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r1.claim: The verb yadmigh means to strike and injure someone so that the brain is opened.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r1.anchor: The verb يدمغ means to strike and injure someone in a way that it opens up the brain

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r2.claim: The respite given to evil alongside truth does not mean equality; it tests which people choose truth and which cling to evil.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r2.anchor: it is not because both are equal

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r3.claim: Truth will strike evil decisively and destroy it at once, like a blow to the brain that immediately kills.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r3.anchor: just as a decisive blow on the brain gives immediate death to a person

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r4.claim: The condemned words include their claims that the world is sport and that polytheistic intercession can protect them; these beliefs bring ruin.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r4.anchor: refer to their view that this world is a place of sport and recreation

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r5.speaker: idolaters
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r5.claim: They expected their deities and intercessors to rescue them from danger in the hereafter, so they felt no fear of it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p105/r5.anchor: they reckoned that if ever the hereafter comes, their deities and intercessors will save them from every danger

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p23/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p23/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p23/r1.claim: Qatada glosses the vanishing of falsehood as its perishing.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p23/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فإذا هو زاهق ﴾ قال هالك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r4.claim: Mujahid identifies the truth hurled at falsehood as the Qur’an and falsehood as Satan; he says every Qur’anic use of falsehood means Satan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r4.anchor: وهو الشيطان قاله مجاهد، وقال كل ما في القرآن من الباطل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r5.claim: Another view takes truth as proof that defeats falsehood, including their false descriptions of God as having a child.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r5.anchor: بالحجة على الباطل وهو شبههم ووصفهم الله بغير صفاته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r6.claim: A broader interpretation makes truth Qur’an, messengerhood, and law, and falsehood the corresponding general opposite.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: الحق عام في القرآن والرسالة والشرع، والباطل أيضا عام كذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r7.claim: بل shifts away from the idea of play: truth demolishes falsehood, vividly likened to a hard object striking and killing a hollow body.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r7.anchor: استعار لذلك القذف والدمغ تصويرا لإبطاله وإهداره ومحقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r8.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r8.claim: Isa ibn Umar reads فيدمغه with an accusative final غ; al-Zamakhshari calls this weak and compares it with a poetic line ending فأستريحا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر فيدمغه بنصب الغين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r9.claim: A further reading has a ḍamma on the mīm in فيدمغه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r10.claim: The threat of woe addresses disbelievers for attributing a consort, child, and other impossible qualities to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r10.anchor: أي الخزي والهم مما تصفون أي تصفونه مما لا يليق به تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r11.claim: Another view addresses those who deny messengers and call the Qur’an magic or confused dreams; Abu Hayyan rejects as remote the proposed shift from third-person to direct address.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p415#2/r11.anchor: وأبعد من ذهب إلى أنه التفات من ضمير الغيبة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r1.claim: Bal turns from the denial that God intends play to the positive claim that His way is to make serious truth overcome play-like falsehood; this point leads into the coming threat.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r1.anchor: إضراب على اتخاذ اللهو واللعب بل عن إرادة الإتخاذ كأنه قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies the truth with the Quran and falsehood with Satan.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد أن الحق القرآن والباطل الشيطان

ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r3.claim: Another view makes truth the proof and falsehood their claims and their description of God with attributes such as having a child; the author prefers the general reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r3.anchor: وقيل الحق الحجة والباطل شبههم ووصفهم الله تعالى بغير صفاته

ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r4.claim: Qadhf originally means a forceful, distant throw, and is metaphorically used for bringing truth against falsehood.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r4.anchor: وأصل القذف الرمي البعيد كما قال الراغب وهو مستلزم لصلابة الرمي

ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r5.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r5.claim: Al-Raghib explains qadhf as distant throwing, entailing a hard impact.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r5.anchor: كما قال الراغب وهو مستلزم لصلابة الرمي

ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r6.claim: Damagha means completely destroying; its original sense is cracking a soft, hollow object, extended metaphorically to annihilation.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r6.anchor: أي يمحقه بالكلية كما فعلنا بأهل القرى المحكمة وأصل الدمغ

ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r7.claim: The image may be a simile of a hard body thrown on a soft brain to crush it, suggesting truth's height and falsehood's lowliness; alternatively it is a hidden metaphor comparing truth and falsehood to those bodies, but the author prefers the full simile.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r7.anchor: وجوز أيضا أن يكون استعارة مكنية بتشبيه الحق بشيء صلب

ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r8.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r8.claim: Isa ibn Umar reads the verb after fa in the subjunctive; the author notes grammarians reject this construction here because fa does not govern it, and the usual exceptional responses do not apply.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ عيسى ابن عمر ( فيدمغه ) بالنصب وضعف بأن ما بعد الفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r9.claim: A poetic parallel is disputed: the final verb may be an indicative reinforced by a light emphatic nūn, stopped on with alif; this explanation is considered weak, making the verse's subjunctive reading weaker still.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r9.anchor: سأترك منزلي لبني تميم وألحق بالحجاز فأستريحا

ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r10.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r10.claim: Abu al-Baqa takes the subjunctive reading as coordinated with al-haqq, yielding the sense that God casts truth and thereby destroys falsehood.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r10.anchor: والعطف على هذه القراءة على الحق عند أبي البقاء

ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r11.claim: A scholar instead compares the coordination to giving hay and cold water; the author prefers coordination with the underlying sense, doing the throwing and then the crushing.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r11.anchor: وذكر بعض الأفاضل أنه لو جعل من قبيل علفتها تبنا وماء بارد أصح

ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r12.claim: A reading with damma on both mīm and ghayn in yadmaghuhu is also transmitted.

ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r13.claim: The sudden particle and nominal clause in fa-idha huwa zahiq stress the speed and completeness of falsehood's disappearance, as if it had never existed.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p19#2/r13.anchor: وفي إذا الفجائية والجملة الإسمية من الدلالة على كمال المسارعة

ALUSI-FULL:v17p20/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p20/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p20/r1.claim: The warning is for Quraysh or all Arab unbelievers: they too face punishment like those earlier communities.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p20/r1.anchor: وعيد لقريش أو لجميع الكفار من العرب بأن لهم أيضا مثل مالأولئك

ALUSI-FULL:v17p20/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p20/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p20/r2.claim: The phrase may mean because of what you describe, describeable things, or that the ruin itself comes from their descriptions; ma may be a verbal noun, relative pronoun, or adjective.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p20/r2.anchor: وما إما مصدرية أو موصولة أو موصوفة أي ومستقر لكم الويل والهلاك

ALUSI-FULL:v17p20/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p20/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p20/r3.claim: Their punishment is due to attributing to God what does not befit Him, such as a child, and the address is plainly directed to the unbelievers just mentioned.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p20/r3.anchor: من أجل وصفكم له تعالى بما لا يليق بشأنه الجليل تعالى شأنه

ALUSI-FULL:v17p20/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v17p20/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v17p20/r4.claim: It is far-fetched to take the address as turning from absent people to the former inhabitants of ruined towns, based on what their plea had been.
ALUSI-FULL:v17p20/r4.anchor: وأبعد كل البعد من قال : إنه خطاب لأهل القرى على طريق الإلتفات

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r9.claim: Bal turns away from their statement as a lie and falsehood; naqdhif means throw or unleash, and haqq means faith.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r9.anchor: {بل} أي دع ذلك الذي قالوا فإنه كذب وباطل، {نقذف} نرمي ونسلط، {بالحق} بالإيمان،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r10.claim: An alternative identifies the truth as God's word that He has no child, and falsehood as their claim that He took a child.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r10.anchor: وقيل: الحق قول الله، أنه لا ولد له، والباطل قولهم اتخذ الله ولدا،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r11.claim: Yadmaghu means destroy; its root image is a head wound reaching the brain. Zahiq means gone, as falsehood vanishes when truth is made clear.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r11.anchor: {فيدمغه} فيهلكه، وأصل الدمغ: شج الرأس حتى يبلغ الدماغ، {فإذا هو زاهق} ذاهب،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r12.claim: The verse threatens disbelievers for describing God with what is unfitting, such as a spouse or child.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r12.anchor: {ولكم الويل} يا معشر الكفار، {مما تصفون} الله بما لا يليق به من الصاحبة والولد.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r13.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p313/r13.claim: Mujahid glosses what they describe as their lies.

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:18/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:18/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:18/r1.claim: The statement turns from play and declares God's transcendence of play: His way is to overcome falsehood with truth, including earnestness over amusement.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:18/r1.anchor: إضراب عن اتخاذ اللهو وتنزيه لذاته عن اللعب أي بل من شأننا أن نغلب الحق الذي من جملته الجد على الباطل

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:18/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:18/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:18/r2.claim: Yadmaghuhu means crush it; the metaphor of a hard, far-reaching throw and crushing the brain vividly depicts falsehood's destruction and death.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:18/r2.anchor: فيمحقه، وإنما استعار لذلك القذف وهو الرمي البعيد المستلزم لصلابة المرمى، والدمغ الذي هو كسر الدماغ

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:18/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:18/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:18/r3.claim: A reading makes yadmaghahu subjunctive; despite the distance it is parsed by meaning or coordinated with al-ḥaqq, as an anonymous poem illustrates.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:18/r3.anchor: وقرىء { فيدمغه } بالنصب كقوله: سأترك منزلي لبني تميم

BAYDAWI-FULL:21:18/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:18/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:18/r4.claim: Zāhiq means perished; the language of the departing soul sustains the death metaphor, and woe is due to impermissible descriptions of God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:21:18/r4.anchor: هالك والزهوق ذهاب الروح وذكره لترشيح المجاز. { ولكم الويل مما تصفون } مما تصفونه به مما لا يجوز عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p73/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p73/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p73/r4.claim: God casts the revealed, steadfast Qur'anic truth against falsehood as a solid rock against a hollow body, smashing falsehood and making it vanish immediately.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p73/r4.anchor: تصويرا للحق بجعل الحق كأنه جرم صلب كالصخرة قذف بها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p73/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p73/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p73/r5.claim: The Qur'an contains argument and firmness, with no frivolity or falsehood; it destroys the falsehood people invent about it and other matters.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p73/r5.anchor: هذا الذكر الحكيم الذي أنزلناه جدال كله وثباتا جميعه لا لهو فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p73/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p73/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p73/r6.claim: Woe is due for describing everything according to whim without divine warrant, since people do not grasp realities; truth exposes false descriptions of the Qur'an, God, and the world.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p73/r6.anchor: من وصفكم لكل شيء بما تهوى أنفسكم من غير إذن منا لكم

DURR-FULL:v5p619/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p619/r13.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p619/r13.claim: The Quran is truth cast against confusion, making falsehood perish.
DURR-FULL:v5p619/r13.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {بل نقذف بالحق} قال: القرآن {على الباطل} قال: اللبس {فإذا هو زاهق} قال: هالك

DURR-FULL:v5p620/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p620/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p620/r1.claim: The curse for false descriptions applies to every liar until the Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v5p620/r1.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله: {ولكم الويل مما تصفون} قال: هي والله لكل واصف كذب إلى يوم القيامة

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولبعضالعرب#306/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولبعضالعرب#306/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولبعضالعرب#306/r1.claim: Sībawayh distinguishes the open lām of vocative يا ويل لك from the ordinary genitive lām; without yāʾ the lām returns to its regular form, as in لكم الويل.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولبعضالعرب#306/r1.anchor: وعلى ذلك قال أبو عمرو يا ويل لك ويا ويح لك كأنه نبه إنسانا ثم جعل

SIBAWAYH:هذابابمايعملفيالأفعالفيجزمها)#4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:هذابابمايعملفيالأفعالفيجزمها)#4.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:هذابابمايعملفيالأفعالفيجزمها)#4.claim: Jussive particles govern verbs, and jussive inflection occurs only in imperfect verbs; Sībawayh compares jussive in verbs to genitive in nouns.
SIBAWAYH:هذابابمايعملفيالأفعالفيجزمها)#4.anchor: واعلم أن حروف الجزم لا ~~تجزم إلا الأفعال ولا يكون الجزم إلا في هذه الأفعال المضارعة للأسماء

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p296#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p296#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p296#2/r1.claim: Wayl is a comprehensive word for every kind of evil; al-Aṣmaʿī calls it a term of condemnation.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p296#2/r1.anchor: الويل: كلمة جامعة للشر كله. قال الأصمعي: ويل تقبيح

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p296#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p296#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p296#2/r2.claim: The Arabs also use al-alīl for groaning.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p296#2/r2.anchor: تقول العرب: له الويل، والأليل والأليل: الأنين

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p296#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p296#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p296#2/r3.claim: The expression may convey regret and grief, as in يا ويلنا and يا ويلتى; ويح and ويس are diminutive forms.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p296#2/r3.anchor: وقد توضع في موضع التحسر والتفجع، كقوله: يا ويلنا

DURR-FULL:v1p17/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r1.claim: A man saw Umar praying at night with al-Fatiha alone, then glorifying God, bowing, and prostrating; Umar called this the prayer of angels.
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r1.anchor: عن أبي المنهال سيار بن سلامة أن عمر بن الخطاب سقط عليه رجل من المهاجرين وعمر يتهجد من الليل يقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب

DURR-FULL:v1p17/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r2.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r2.claim: Al-Suyuti infers from the anecdote that angels were permitted to recite al-Fatiha alone.
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r2.anchor: قلت: فيه أن الملائكة أذن لهم في قراءة الفاتحة فقط

DURR-FULL:v1p17/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r3.speaker: ابن الصلاح
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r3.claim: Ibn al-Salah says Qur'an recitation is a privilege granted to humans rather than angels, who are eager to hear humans recite.
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r3.anchor: فقد ذكر ابن الصلاح أن قراءة القرآن خصيصة أوتيها البشر دون الملائكة وأنهم حريصون على سماعه من الإنس

DURR-FULL:v1p17/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r4.claim: Abu Qilaba reports from the Prophet that whoever hears al-Fatiha opened receives the merit of witnessing a battle in God's cause, and hearing it completed is like witnessing the spoils distributed.
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r4.anchor: عن أبي قلابة يرفعه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: من شهد فاتحة الكتاب حين يستفتح كان كمن شهد فتحا في سبيل الله

DURR-FULL:v1p17/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r5.claim: The Prophet says whoever recites al-Fatiha and another sura before sleeping will have an angel assigned to accompany him when he wakes.
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r5.anchor: عن شداد بن أوس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا أخذ أحدكم مضجعه ليرقد فليقرأ بأم القرآن وسورة

DURR-FULL:v1p17/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r6.claim: The Prophet rules that there is no prayer for one who does not recite al-Fatiha.
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r6.anchor: عن عبادة بن الصامت أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لا صلاة لمن لم يقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب

DURR-FULL:v1p17/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r7.claim: The Prophet says the Mother of the Qur'an substitutes for other recitation, while nothing else substitutes for it.
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r7.anchor: عن عبادة بن الصامت قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أم القرآن عوض عن غيرها وليس غيرها عوضا عنها

DURR-FULL:v1p17/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r8.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's warning that a prayer without al-Fatiha is deficient or deceptive.
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: أمرني رسول الله قال كل صلاة لايقرأ فيها بفاتحة الكتاب فهي خداع

DURR-FULL:v1p17/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r9.claim: The Prophet repeats that a prayer without the Mother of the Book is deficient three times.
DURR-FULL:v1p17/r9.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من صلى صلاة لم يقرأ فيها بأم الكتاب فهي خداج فهي خداج ثلاث مرات

JISHUMI:v1p860/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p860/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p860/r1.claim: The verse refutes necessary knowledge: if knowledge were necessary, everyone would form one community and disagreement could not occur.
JISHUMI:v1p860/r1.anchor: الآية تدل على بطلان قول أصحاب المعارف؛ لأنها لو كانت ضرورية لكان الناس أمة واحدة

JISHUMI:v1p860/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p860/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p860/r2.claim: It refutes determinism because sending prophets presupposes that people can move from unbelief to faith.
JISHUMI:v1p860/r2.anchor: وتدل على بطلان القول بالجبر؛ لأن بعثه الأنبياء إليهم توجب صحة انتقالهم من الكفر إلى الإيمان

JISHUMI:v1p860/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p860/r3.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p860/r3.claim: Abu Ali takes the scope as particular: each era has some witnesses for truth, even if few; broad wording fits because unbelief predominates.
JISHUMI:v1p860/r3.anchor: قال أبو علي: المراد به الخصوص، ولأن كل زمان لا بد فيه من شهداء يقومون بالحق

JISHUMI:v1p860/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p860/r4.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v1p860/r4.claim: The Qadi says Abu Ali’s argument follows if every era has a truth-speaker, but that is unproved.
JISHUMI:v1p860/r4.anchor: وقال القاضي: إن ثبت أن في كل زمان من قائل بالحق على ما يذهب إليه أبو علي

JISHUMI:v1p860/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p860/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p860/r5.claim: The verse permits that all people could be unbelievers with no truth-speaker; Islamic law rules this out by transmitted proof that consensus leaves no era without people affirming truth.
JISHUMI:v1p860/r5.anchor: وتدل الآية على أنه يجوز أن يكون الناس كلهم كفارا ليس فيهم قائل بالحق

ITQAN:v2p526#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p526#2/r1.speaker: الأصمعي
ITQAN:v2p526#2/r1.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says ويل is a word of reproach.
ITQAN:v2p526#2/r1.anchor: قال الأصمعي ويل تقبيح قال تعالى ﴿ ولكم الويل مما تصفون ﴾

ITQAN:v2p526#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p526#2/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p526#2/r2.claim: ويل can also express grief and distress, as in يا ويلتنا and يا ويلتى.
ITQAN:v2p526#2/r2.anchor: وقد يوضع موضع التحسر والتفجع نحو ﴿ يا ويلتنا ﴾ ﴿ يا ويلتى أعجزت ﴾

ITQAN:v2p526#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p526#2/r3.speaker: عائشة
ITQAN:v2p526#2/r3.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet reassured her that ويحك or ويسك expresses mercy, so she should fear ويل instead.
ITQAN:v2p526#2/r3.anchor: عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة قالت قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ويحك
